recipe.notes:
Engine. The released image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0 cannot serve this checkpoint: vLLM v0.31.0 has no EmbeddingGemma2Model in its registry, its requirements pin transformers <5.18.0 and the image carries 5.17.0, which has no embedding_gemma2 config or processor; and vLLM v0.31.0 has no Gemma video backend. The architecture landed in vLLM commit 02b83919aa2e (PR #60254, 2026-10-06) and the checkpoint's classes in transformers 5.19.0 (released 2026-10-06). Decision 38: this recipe pins the nightly by digest. E2 r1 (the first wave on this image): serve failed -- the digest-pinned nightly's own transformers does NOT carry the embedding_gemma2 classes (AutoConfig refuses the checkpoint's config.json and vLLM's embedding_gemma2 model module cannot import them), so the wave's first fix is this recipe's fold: `serve.plugin: rcp-ndcg-vllm` installs the plugin wheel and `serve.patches: [embeddinggemma2-transformers-fold]` opts into the patch that loads transformers 5.19.0's three embedding_gemma2 modules (configuration, processing, video processing) from the wheel under their upstream module names and registers the config class with AutoConfig and the processor and video-processor classes with AutoProcessor/AutoVideoProcessor; vLLM's own registry carries the model class. The patch is inert when the image's transformers already has the classes (it probes the import first), and it is verified on CPU against transformers 5.17.0: the checkpoint's config.json parses, the processor loads, and text, image and video calls all return tensors. SWITCH TO RELEASE / REMOVAL: needs vLLM commit 02b83919aa2e (PR #60254) and transformers >= 5.19.0; switch engine.image to the first vLLM release that carries both, delete `serve.plugin`, `plugin_architectures` and `patches`, and re-validate. The wave records the image's actual transformers version in its provenance.
Frame. The model reads its input through no frame at all: the checkpoint's chat_template.jinja renders a message's text and media placeholders in order and adds nothing (no role markers, no default system turn). The card's task prompt is a per-encode prefix (prompt_name="SearchQuery"/"Document"), so the client applies it through query_prompt/doc_prompt and the declared template is content-only (its fixed segments are none, and the messages route sends the content alone). The tokenizer's post-processor adds BOS and EOS around every render (declared with add_special_tokens: true), and mean pooling over every token (the checkpoint's Pooling module: mean, include_prompt true) is the embedding: no anchor token exists, so a cut only has to keep the content it cuts, and the prompt prefix is reserved because it sits at the head of the content.
Media. Images: the checkpoint's Gemma4ImageProcessor resizes every image to at most 280 soft tokens (max_patches = 280 x 3^2 = 2,520 patches, both edges a multiple of patch x pooling = 48) -- the resize scales a 16x16 icon up to 768x768 and a 2480x3508 page down to 672x912 -- and the prompt gets boi + 280-or-fewer soft tokens + eoi. The client reproduces the resize (the gemma4 processor geometry in rcp_ndcg.data.resolution) and counts the pooled patches plus the two markers. No engine pin is needed: the checkpoint's processor_config.json carries the 280 budget, which is what a stock nightly engine loads; the client declares the same number. Videos: the engine samples by fps, capped at max_frames (it ignores num_frames: video.py:422-523), so the recipe pins 60 fps and 32 frames with --media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"fps": 60, "max_frames": 32}}', which realizes the declared 32 uniformly spaced frames for any clip of at least 32/60 s (the client's own frame-count check admits a container only with at least 32 frames, so a normal clip passes above that). The card's default is 1 fps and declares the rate configurable; this recipe's declared instrument is the 32-frame cap. The prompt renders one boi + 140-or-fewer soft tokens + eoi block PER FRAME (no temporal patch), so the client counts frames x (per-frame patches + 2). The media wave must confirm the engine's sampled count and token count on a real clip; a clip whose frame rate exceeds 60 fps and whose duration is under 0.53 s can make the engine sample fewer than 32 (the one declared open corner).
Budgets. client.max_tokens 8192 is the card's 8K context, counted as the engine sees the whole prompt (BOS + prefix + content + EOS, plus any media tokens reserved whole); the content span is cut (on_overflow: cut) and the frame re-attached, so the prefix survives. The card's own ST path truncates the assembled prompt right at max_seq_length inside encode; the reference renders the full prompt and declares over_cap_cut_differs, so over-cap rows ride the non-gating table and under-cap rows gate exactly. dtype bfloat16 (the card's rule; never float16). empty_doc: send -- the card embeds an empty document as its bare document prompt, which is the empty string under the prefix. The 32-bit offset fault (a 262144-token warmup) and the exactly-max_model_len pooling hang (observed at 32768) do not arise at this recipe's 8192 cap: the engine's warmup is one 8192-token sequence -- the pairs' length:at_budget row (8188 tokens) and the wave's smoke exercise the boundary. Media outputs (stage 2 compares them): the reference's embed mode reads the harness's `media` field -- a media side becomes a one-user-turn conversation with the parts in order (the card injects the declared prompt as its system message, which the checkpoint's template renders first), an image a loaded PIL image, and a container handed to the checkpoint's own video processor with the declared pin (fps 60, the 32-frame cap and the checkpoint's own uniform overflow strategy: video_processing_kwargs) -- transformers 5.19.0's EmbeddingGemma2VideoProcessor.sample_frames consumes all three and reproduces the digest-pinned engine's EmbeddingGemma2VideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample exactly (W2 re-verification: the shipped rows give [0, 0, 2, 3, ...], where the product's generic uniform rule would give [0, 1, 2, ...]), so the reference never samples with the generic rule -- and computes the card's vectors for media rows exactly as for text rows, so stage 2 gates them by the same cosine rule; the media stage still gates placement, geometry and tokens.
MRL. The card's Matryoshka set {128, 256, 512, 768} is declared once, in the client's mrl_kind/mrl_dims and in serve.hf_overrides (the engine refuses a per-request dimensions without is_matryoshka, and the checkpoint declares neither key). The recipe ships the full 768-wide vector; a run selects k from the declared set (engine-side `dimensions` or the client-side mrl_dim), and the GPU wave gates each declared k (the stage-2 ex-post cut) -- the 768 is the model's own projected output, so both paths are the card's truncation order.
